work.permit: Individual permit under the Minister of Labour's system for artistic performances

note: Work: Labour Act, 2017 (Act No. 64, Juba, 24 October 2017, as printed by the Ministry of Justice; the copy FAOLEX holds), section 12: it applies to all work by children, employed or not; no one may engage a child under 14 (the subsection's wording ties the bar to the 'worst forms' of section 13, but the section is headed 'Minimum Working Age' and the light-work exception from 12 only makes sense against a general age of 14, so 14 is held, a reading); a child of 12 may do light work the Minister specifies; no one under 18 does hazardous work (16 by regulation for some categories). Subsection (8) lets the Minister, after consultation, establish a system by which a person may obtain a permit to engage a child under 14 for such purposes as artistic performances, granted individually with conditions and limited hours (subsection 9). Whether the Minister has set up that system wasn't read; no lower age is set. The Child Act, 2008 (section 25) wasn't read. Majority and service: not read; no South Sudanese statute setting the age of majority or calling anyone to military service was reached (southsudanlii.org didn't answer).

sources.title: Laws of South Sudan, Labour Act, 2017 (Act No. 64), printed by the Ministry of Justice (copy held by FAOLEX)
sources.said: 12. Minimum Working Age (1) This section shall apply to all forms of work performed by children, whether or not the child is an employee. (2) Subject to the provisions of sub-section (3) this section, no person shall engage or permit the engagement of a child under the age of 14 years ... a child who has attained the age of twelve years may be engaged to perform light work ... the Minister may establish a system by which a person might obtain a permit to engage a child under the age of fourteen years for such purposes as participation in artistic performances. (9) The permits provided for in sub-section (8) shall be granted on an individual basis
